patterns.rationale: Catches the phrase "environment variables" in each payload's language: French `variables d'environnement` (Miss 1), German `Umgebungszugriffsfunktion` (Miss 2), Spanish `variables de entorno` (Miss 3), Portuguese `variáveis de ambiente` (Miss 4), Turkish `ortam değişken` (Miss 5). All five payloads' core attack action is reading env vars; these are the language-specific signals the English-only static layer cannot see. `d[e']\s*` handles both `de ` and `d'` contractions.
patterns.fp_notes: These phrases could appear in legitimately multilingual documentation, but the known-good corpus is English-only; none of these terms appear there.

patterns.rationale: Every payload opens with an explicit "instruction to the automated AI" framing in its respective language. These phrases are the non-English analogue of English authority-injection openers: French `Note de traitement pour l'assistant automatisé`, German `Konfigurationshinweis für automatisierte Verarbeitung`, Spanish `Nota para el sistema de análisis automatizado`, Portuguese `instrução para processamento automatizado por IA`, Turkish `Yapay zeka işleme talimatı`. This closes the multilingual AUTHORITY gap without touching any English alternation. `f[uü]r` handles both ASCII-folded and proper umlaut.
patterns.fp_notes: None — these compound constructions ("processing note for the automated assistant", "configuration hint for automated processing") have no legitimate use in English codebases; even multilingual docs would not assemble these exact phrases.

patterns.rationale: Catches the Spanish authority-override in Miss 3: `las instrucciones operativas previas no son aplicables` ("prior operating instructions are not applicable"). This is semantically identical to `ignore previous instructions` but phrased as a negated-applicability statement in Spanish — a known social-engineering alternative to the imperative form that evades all existing `_AUTHORITY_RE` alternations. `{0,3}` tolerates an intervening adjective like `operativas`.
patterns.fp_notes: None — the construction "prior instructions are not applicable" has no plausible use in code documentation.

patterns.rationale: Catches multilingual credential-exfiltration vocabulary missing from the English-only static layer. German `Zugangsdaten` (access credentials) and `Authentifizierungstoken` (authentication tokens) appear in Miss 2's explicit data-collection instruction. Portuguese `credenciais de serviços/nuvem/acesso` and `tokens de autenticação` appear in Miss 4's cloud-credential collection instruction. These are high-signal terms for credential exfil that the English `transmit.*credential` pattern cannot reach. `servi[çc]` handles both `serviços` and `servicios`.
patterns.fp_notes: `Zugangsdaten` and `Authentifizierungstoken` are standard German IT terms that could appear in German documentation; `credenciais de` is standard Portuguese. Neither will appear in the English-only known-good corpus. Word-boundary anchors on the German terms prevent partial matches.

semantic_note: N/A — all five payloads contain distinctive foreign-language vocabulary (env-var terms, credential terms, AI-directive framing) that anchors narrow regex patterns without over-generalising.
